query: What should I do if my car won't start?
generated_text:
If your 2020 Corolla won't start, let's go through some steps to diagnose the issue. First, check if the dashboard lights come on when you turn the key. If they don't, it's likely a dead battery. In this case, you can try jump-starting the car. Make sure to follow proper jump-starting procedures to avoid any damage to the electrical system.

If the dashboard lights do come on, but the car won't start, it could be a faulty starter or a problem with the fuel delivery system. Listen for any clicking sounds when you turn the key. If you hear a clicking sound, it might indicate a starter issue. If you don't hear any sounds, it could be a problem with the ignition system or the fuel pump.

It's also possible that the issue is related to the spark plugs or the fuel filter. A clogged fuel filter or worn-out spark plugs can prevent the engine from starting. 

To further diagnose the issue, you can try to crank the engine and see if it turns over. If it cranks but doesn't start, it could be a problem with the fuel system, such as a faulty fuel pump or a clogged fuel injector.

If you're not comfortable troubleshooting the issue yourself, it's recommended to have a professional mechanic inspect the ignition and fuel systems to determine the root cause of the problem. They can perform tests and inspections to identify the issue and provide a proper repair.

Remember to always prioritize your safety and the safety of others when working with vehicles. If you're unsure about any aspect of the diagnosis or repair, it's best to seek the help of a qualified mechanic.
reference_text: If your car won't start, the most common causes are a dead battery, a faulty starter, or an empty fuel tank. First, check if your headlights and interior lights work; if they are dim or dead, your battery is likely the issue. You can try jump-starting it.

query: How do I check my car's oil level?
generated_text:
To check your car's oil level, you'll want to make sure the engine is turned off and the vehicle is parked on a level surface. Locate the oil dipstick, which is usually labeled "Oil" or have an oil can symbol on it. Pull out the dipstick and wipe it clean with a lint-free cloth or paper towel. Insert the dipstick back into the oil reservoir and pull it out again. The dipstick will now be coated with oil, and you can check the oil level by looking at the end of the dipstick.

The oil level should be between the "MIN" and "MAX" marks on the dipstick. If the level is below the "MIN" mark, you'll need to add oil to the engine. Be sure to use the correct type of oil for your vehicle, which can be found in your owner's manual.

It's also a good idea to check the oil color and consistency. If the oil is dark or dirty, it may be a sign that the oil is dirty and needs to be changed. If you're unsure about how to check the oil level or what type of oil to use, it's always best to consult your owner's manual or speak with a professional mechanic.

In your case, since you have a 2020 Corolla with a petrol engine, you can refer to your owner's manual for specific instructions on how to check the oil level. If you have any further questions or concerns, feel free to ask.
reference_text: To check your oil level, park the car on level ground and wait for the engine to cool down. Pull out the dipstick, wipe it clean with a rag, insert it all the way back in, and then pull it out again. The oil level should be between the 'Full' and 'Add' (or 'F' and 'L') marks.
